topics.topic: CLK-001 clock-read count and timestamp semantics for audited mutations
questions: For a mutation that appends an audit record, must the CLK-001 test count one wall-source read or two, and must occurred_at equal the operation instant or the audit writer's later instant?
For an audited mutation, must the test observe one wall-clock-source call for the whole call graph, or one operation call plus one separately attributed audit-writer call?

judgement.why: This is the same question previously judged about the operation's one wall reading plus the audit writer's separately attributed further reading, and the relevant A28 passages have not changed since that judgement.

precedent.topic: Wall-clock read count for an audited operation including its audit writer
quotes:
An operation
reads the clock once for its own timestamps, and that one
instant supplies every portal-owned timestamp it writes (event times such as
`created_at`, `received_at`, `revoked_at`) and every current-time comparison
that decides the validity of those writes or of persisted records.

The one exception is the `occurred_at` of an audit record appended
through the audit writer: the writer takes it when it appends (Factory
code `application/audit_writer.py` 136); the bootstrap, which builds its
own audit, keeps its one instant.

- the wall clock gives the instant: the current UTC time as an offset-naive
  datetime, one reading per operation for its own timestamps, the same value
  `datetime.utcnow()` gives (no cache, no local time, no second reading by
  the operation, no arithmetic in the clock source; an operation derives
  an expiry by adding its TTL to the instant it read); the audit writer's reading of an appended
  record's `occurred_at` is the one further reading (the exception above);
precedent.why: An audited timestamp-writing operation produces two clock-source calls: the operation's single reading and the audit writer's explicitly separate further reading, except for bootstrap's named one-instant behavior.

topics.topic: CLK-001 wall-clock sharing across authorization guards and admitted operations
questions: Must a request that authenticates a session and then performs a timestamped mutation share one wall-clock reading across the guard and mutation, or may each module-level operation take its own reading?
What is the operation boundary that must share one wall-clock reading, particularly between expiry validation in an authorization guard and the authorized read or mutation it admits?

judgement.why: This repeats the previously judged question about whether authorization and the admitted mutation share one operation-level wall reading, with no change to the passages deciding it.

precedent.topic: Boundary of a single operation sharing one wall-clock reading
quotes:
An operation is what another module, the
HTTP route table or the host may call; everything else a module does is
hidden.

- **Time.** Only `system_clock` reads the host clocks (A28). An operation
  that needs the current instant takes one wall reading from it and reuses
  it; the transport guard takes the elapsed reading for the viewer-entry
  window from it. No other module reads a host clock.

_authorize_project_operation: [BEHAVIOR] MUST read the current UTC time once per operation, by one call of utc_now, and use that single instant for every timestamp it writes and every current-time comparison it makes; it MUST NOT read a host clock itself.
precedent.why: State 5 defines the operation boundary as each callable public operation, and the later notes give authorization itself its own one-read rule, so a request-wide authorization-plus-mutation reading is not implied.

topics.topic: The candidate-version and expense-allocation condition that causes activation refusal
questions: Exactly which candidate-version/allocation relationship makes activation fail under this Required tests item?
Is activation refused only when an existing expense allocation targets a PortalSection absent from the candidate version, or whenever the candidate has a section to which no expense is allocated?

quotes:
5. `capability:budget_management.activate_budget_version` requires the
   activation capability, refuses while any existing allocation would lose its
   section, deactivates the prior active version, activates the requested one
   and appends `snapshot.activate`, all in one transaction.
judgement.why: The later flow explicitly makes refusal depend on an existing allocation whose section would be absent from the requested version, not on an unallocated candidate section.

topics.topic: Whether idempotent snapshot re-publication permits any persistent writes
questions: Does “changes nothing” mean only that the existing ApprovedEstimateSnapshot is unchanged, or that no persistent record is added?
Does “changes nothing” mean only that the existing ApprovedEstimateSnapshot is unchanged, or that the replay writes no records at all?

quotes:
a
  re-publication of its identity with the same content changes nothing,

An
attempt the import classifies — accepted, idempotent replay, integrity
conflict, or a rejection — is recorded as a fresh immutable import result
with a fresh `import_id` and its `snapshot.import` audit;
judgement.why: The Required test's unqualified no-change outcome conflicts with the product rule requiring two new persistent records for every classified idempotent replay.

bases.passage:
a
  re-publication of its identity with the same content changes nothing,

An
attempt the import classifies — accepted, idempotent replay, integrity
conflict, or a rejection — is recorded as a fresh immutable import result
with a fresh `import_id` and its `snapshot.import` audit;

unsupported_sides:
An
attempt the import classifies — accepted, idempotent replay, integrity
conflict, or a rejection — is recorded as a fresh immutable import result
with a fresh `import_id` and its `snapshot.import` audit;

witness.initial: An accepted snapshot and its publication identity and fingerprint already exist.
events: The same producer republishes identical content for that publication identity.
outcomes: The replay changes nothing, so no persistent import result or audit is added.
The replay leaves the snapshot unchanged but adds a fresh immutable import result with a fresh import_id and a snapshot.import audit.
witness.observer: The producer reading the returned import_id and an administrator inspecting audit history.
basis:
A producer that lost an
answer re-publishes the same snapshot: identical content is answered as an
idempotent replay with a new `import_id` naming the same accepted snapshot
(accepted notes `_build_import_record`, `import_snapshot`; Factory code
`application/snapshot_import.py`).

topics.topic: Behavior when activating the already-active BudgetVersion
questions: Is activation of the already-active BudgetVersion refused, treated as an idempotent no-op, or performed again with new activation provenance and audit?

quotes:
Activating the version that is already
active is no status transition (its status stays `active`) and is not
refused: it records a new activation time and actor for it, deactivates
nothing and is audited like any activation.
judgement.why: The later public-operation contract explicitly requires successful repeated activation with refreshed provenance and audit, rather than refusal or a no-op.

topics.topic: How offset-aware source-supplied timestamps are normalized for storage
questions: For an offset-aware supplied datetime, must storage normalize it to the equivalent offset-naive UTC wall value, or strip/preserve the supplied wall fields?

judgement.why: This is the same previously judged normalization question: preserving the supplied instant requires conversion to offset-naive UTC, while accepted wire forms and checks belong to State 6.

precedent.topic: Accepted and normalized forms of source-supplied datetimes
quotes:
Times a
source supplies — `approved_at`, `published_at` of a snapshot, `confirmed_at`
of a recognition, `photo_date`, a service credential's `expires_at` — are
kept as supplied: the same instant, stored offset-naive UTC like every
persisted timestamp, never replaced by the clock (State 1 Modeling
conventions). Calendar dates a source supplies — `document_date` of a
recognition, `payment_date` — are `date` values, kept as the supplied
calendar day: they carry no time or offset, are never converted to an
instant and never replaced by the clock's day; their accepted forms and checks, and where in an operation
its one clock read happens, are the accepted spec's, carried to States 6–7.
precedent.why: The passage already makes “stored as supplied” preserve the instant while normalizing storage to offset-naive UTC, while the accepted wire representations and validation checks are formats and field-type contracts owned by State 6.

topics.topic: Whether CLK-002 requires exactly one monotonic-clock read per viewer-entry request
questions: Must CLK-002 and its Required tests demonstrate exactly one monotonic-clock-source read per viewer-entry request?

quotes:
- the elapsed clock gives a duration scale: one reading per request of a
  clock that cannot move backwards, in seconds as a float, the same value
  `time.monotonic()` gives. It measures the viewer-entry rate-limit window of
  A25 only; a reading is never stored, never turned into an instant and
  never ordered against a persisted record.

- CLK-002: elapsed durations are measured only through the clock source's
  monotonic reading; they are used within one process, never persisted,
  and never compared with or mixed into wall-clock values. Owner: the
  clock source.

- CLK-002: a test showing that the elapsed durations the portal measures
  (the A25 viewer-entry window) come from the clock source's monotonic
  reading, are not persisted, and are not compared with or mixed into
  wall-clock values.
judgement.divergence: One implementation reads the monotonic source exactly once per viewer-entry request and reuses that value; another reads it separately while pruning, checking and recording, and a clock spy and boundary-time caller observe different calls and rate-limit decisions.
judgement.why: Although the normative rule requires one elapsed reading per request, neither CLK-002 nor its Required tests item says that the test must demonstrate that read-count requirement.

witness.initial: A viewer-entry rate-limit bucket exists and the monotonic source advances between successive reads near a window boundary.
events: A viewer submits one entry request.
The rate limiter prunes the bucket, checks its remaining count and, if admitted, records the attempt.
outcomes: One monotonic value is read and reused for pruning, checking and recording.
Separate monotonic values are read for those steps, allowing the window boundary to move during the request.
witness.observer: The viewer at the rate-limit boundary and a deterministic clock-source spy.
basis:
- the elapsed clock gives a duration scale: one reading per request of a
  clock that cannot move backwards, in seconds as a float, the same value
  `time.monotonic()` gives. It measures the viewer-entry rate-limit window of
  A25 only; a reading is never stored, never turned into an instant and
  never ordered against a persisted record.

topics.topic: Whether a previously deactivated BudgetVersion may be reactivated
questions: May a deactivated BudgetVersion be reactivated later?

quotes:
BudgetVersionStatus: inactive → active → inactive (re-activation allowed
                  while the project is active; ≤1 active per project;
                  each activation sets activated_at/activated_by and clears
                  deactivated_at, each deactivation sets deactivated_at and
                  keeps activated_at/activated_by of the last activation)
judgement.why: The State 2 transition table expressly permits reactivation while the project is active.
